item.title: BOYS BASKETBALL: Rose, Antoniacci lead No. 2 Riverside past No. 1 Dunmore
item.description: DUNMORE – Brayden Rose and Nico Antoniacci made sure the only celebrating that took place would be on the Riverside sideline and in the team locker room. Driven by an upset loss three weeks ago, Rose and Antoniacci combined for 72 points and powered the second-ranked Vikings to an overwhelming 88-71 win over No. 1 Dunmore on Thursday night in a Lackawanna League boys basketball game. item.title: LOCAL COLLEGES: Macciocco gives Marywood men last-second victory
item.description: Old Forge graduate Joe Macciocco was fouled on a 3-point shot attempt with one second left and sank all three free throws to give the Marywood University men’s basketball team a 73-70 victory at Immaculata University on Thursday in Atlantic East Conference action. Marywood led by as many as 21 points early in the second half and had a 16-point lead with 8½ minutes left when Immaculata scored 11 straight points to spark a 19-3 run that tied the game at 70 with 56 seconds left. item.title: BOYS BASKETBALL: Third-quarter run keys Abington Heights’ victory
item.description: Abington Heights used a big third quarter to pull away from Delaware Valley for a 72-50 win Thursday in Lackawanna League Division I boys basketball. Leading by five at halftime, the No. 3 Comets outscored the No. 8 Warriors in the third, 15-5, to extend their advantage to double digits. Andrew Kettel had five points in the quarter, Jordan Shaffer four points while Finn Goldberg and Cooper Manning each hit 3-pointers. item.title: Margie Award presentation at Women’s Resource Center
item.description: The Margie Memorial Award was presented in December at the Women’s Resource Center. The award is presented in the name of Margie Holodnak Davis, a nurse who was murdered by her estranged husband, David Davis, on June 9, 1980. The plaque is given to those who worked tirelessly for the Women’s Resource Center. item.title: Johnson College hosts annual scholarship breakfast
item.description: Alyssa Nicholas, a Johnson College veterinary nursing program student, spoke at the college’s annual scholarship breakfast at Fiorelli Family Catering. During the event, 74 scholarships to the Scranton school were awarded from various community and industry partners.

item.title: HS SWIMMING: Galko leads Scranton Prep past Abington Heights in battle of unbeaten teams
item.description: Sophia Galko won two individual events and was a member of a winning relay to lead Scranton Prep to an 86-80 win over Abington Heights on Thursday night at the University of Scranton in a Lackawanna League girls’ swimming meet in a battle of teams that entered the meet with undefeated records. Galko won the 100-yard butterfly and the 100 backstroke, and teamed with Eva Kaszuba, Ella Schofield, and Anna Millett to win the 200 medley relay for the Classics (7-0). item.title: Flyers find a bumpy landing with loss in Boston
item.description: Problems with their flight from Columbus Wednesday night meant the Flyers didn’t get to bed in Boston until after 4 o'clock Thursday morning. They played like it in a 6-3 loss to the Bruins.
